Full analysis and per-difference reasoning: docs/migration.md.

rules.reason: Runbook's /tags/ and /categories/ BROWSE pages are unpaginated by design (specs/003 §3.4): every term, grouped by initial letter and counted, on one page. Stack paginates them at pagerSize, which on this archive minted /tags/page/2..30/ and /categories/page/2..3/. Those 31 URLs disappear. They are indexed today, so the site must ship 301s (see docs/migration.md §4) — this rule records that the LOSS is intended, not that the redirects are optional.
Hugo mints /page/1/ as a meta-refresh alias to the unpaginated first page. No pagination on the taxonomy browse page means no page/1 to alias. Same root cause as the url rule above.
Consequence of the pages themselves no longer existing, not an independent canonical change. No page that still exists changed its canonical.
Consequence of the pages themselves no longer existing. No page that still exists changed its og:url.

specs/003 §3.7 item 4 — page kinds map to schema types EXPLICITLY. citizix's schema.html emits @type Article for every .IsPage, so a privacy policy and a search page both claimed to be news articles with a mainEntityOfPage. Runbook types them WebPage, which has no mainEntityOfPage. This is a correction; the four URLs are unchanged and still carry BreadcrumbList.

These are <image:loc> values, not page URLs — citizix overrides layouts/sitemap.xml with a Google image-sitemap extension. It fires on `.Params.image`, which exactly two pages in a 1,159-page build carry, and on one of those it emits an empty <image:title/> because `$.Title` inside `range .Data.Pages` resolves to the sitemap page. Runbook uses Hugo's internal sitemap. See docs/migration.md §5 for why the override is classified citizix-only and recommended for deletion rather than porting.

The two taxonomy LIST feeds carry different things in the two themes, by design on Runbook's side (layouts/rss.xml, the `eq .Kind "taxonomy"` branch). Stack ranges the taxonomy's children, which on a taxonomy kind are TERM pages, so /tags/index.xml is 297 links to /tags/{term}/ and /categories/index.xml is 28 links to /categories/{term}/ — a feed whose items are tags, which tells a subscriber that a tag exists rather than that an article was published. Runbook collects the pages carrying any term in that taxonomy, newest first: /tags/index.xml is 488 article permalinks and /categories/index.xml is 491. The two item sets have ZERO overlap, which is why this reports as `changed` on both feeds rather than as a partial edit. Measured consequence worth knowing: every published post on this archive carries a category, so Runbook's /categories/index.xml is set-identical to /index.xml, and /tags/index.xml is that set minus the three posts that carry no tag. Term feeds (/tags/{term}/index.xml) are unaffected and identical on both themes — .RegularPages is correct there. NOT the pair of defects this rule replaces: those were the home feed publishing non-post pages, and both taxonomy feeds shipping EMPTY, and #25 fixed both. The home-feed rule matched nothing at this pin (491 items on both sides) and has been deleted rather than left to rot.
